newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore authorities investigate ex-Merrill banker.
newsitem.headline: Singapore authorities investigate ex-Merrill banker.

text.p: Singapore's Commercial Affairs Department is investigating a former private banker at Merrill Lynch, a Monetary Authority of Singapore official said on Tuesday.
"The CAD is investigating it," he said, in answer to a question at a briefing on the MAS 1996/97 annual report.
The CAD, Singapore's white collar crime unit, has declined to comment on the matter.

U.S. merchant bank Merrill Lynch has said the former employee, Kevin James Wallace, "engaged in unauthorised trading, misrepresenting or falsifying private clients' statements and forging client signatures".
It also said it had started civil proceedings in Singapore and Hong Kong against Wallace and filed a criminal complaint in Singapore.
A lawsuit filed in the Singapore High Court by Merrill against Wallace has been sealed to protect confidential customer accounts.
Merrill has not commented on the amount in question in the case but industry sources and media reports have estimated some US$30 million could be involved.
An industry source described Wallace as "one of the top brokers within Merrill handling huge accounts". Merrill has sought to freeze Wallace's assets internationally.
The whereabouts of Wallace were not known.
Asked earlier at the MAS briefing about regulation of the growing private banking sector in Singapore, the official said it was no different from any other financial activity in Singapore.
As a regulator, it was important to ensure that only reputable institutions and professionals were admitted into the industry, he said.
